# Module `channels`

channels - thread-safe typed message channels for Vyb.

A channel passes Int values between threads (a runtime heap ring-buffer under
a Mutex + CondVar). A default channel is unbounded: chan_send always succeeds
(the buffer grows as needed). chan_bounded(n) fixes the capacity, and a full
bounded send returns 0 immediately (non-blocking), so callers can apply their
own backpressure. chan_recv blocks until a value arrives (or the channel is
closed); chan_try is the non-blocking form for polling/select.

Usage:
  import channels
  ch = chan_new()            // unbounded
  ok = chan_send(ch, 42)     // 1 on success, 0 if closed/full
  v  = chan_recv(ch)         // blocks until 42 arrives

  b = chan_bounded(2)        // fixed capacity
  chan_send(b, 1); chan_send(b, 2)
  chan_send(b, 3)            // 0: buffer is full

The channels compose with practical applications (e.g. a chunked HTTP body, a
pipeline, or an event queue). String payloads / a true `chan<T>` generic type
remain future work.

### `chan_close` · fn

```
chan_close(ch<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Mark `ch` closed and wake any blocked receivers. After close, receivers see
buffered values, then report absent/-1 once drained. Returns 1 or 0.

<a id="sym-chan_recv_opt"></a>
### `chan_recv_opt` · fn

```
chan_recv_opt(ch<Int>)<Int?> ->
```

Lossless blocking recv for `async for` / draining: returns the value wrapped
in a native `Int?` (present when a value arrives, absent when the channel is
closed and drained). Unlike `chan_recv`, no valid Int payload is reserved as a
sentinel.

**Relationships**

- mentions [`chan_recv`](#sym-chan_recv)

<a id="sym-chan_select"></a>
### `chan_select` · fn

```
chan_select(handles<Vec<Int>>)<Int> ->
```

Block until at least one of the channels in `handles` has a value (or is
closed), then return its index without consuming it ("select"). Follow up with
chan_recv(handles[i]) to dequeue. A closed channel is reported as ready so you
can observe closure via a -1 recv. Returns -1 on an empty/bad handle Vec.


Enqueue `v` (non-blocking). Returns 1 on success, or 0 if the channel is
closed or a bounded channel is full.

### `chan_try` · fn

```
chan_try(ch<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Non-blocking dequeue. Returns a buffered value, or -1 if the channel is empty
(or closed). Useful for polling a channel without blocking.
